news.title: U.S. Retail Spending Slows in October
news.summary: American shoppers lifted October retail spending by just 0.2% after a 0.8% gain in September, with autos and furniture both posting declines while card balances climbed to $1.17 trillion.
news.why: Importers stocking for spring should temper reorder volumes on big-ticket categories like furniture and vehicles, where demand is visibly cooling.

news.title: Companies Earmark Millions in Tariff Refunds for Corporate Bonuses
news.summary: An investigation found at least nine firms, including TJX, Acushnet and American Eagle, steering part of their returned tariff payments into executive and staff bonuses.
news.why: If your company paid duties that may be refundable, make sure finance has filed the claims and that suppliers or customers who shared the cost know where the money is going.

news.title: U.S. Senators Urge FAA to Pause New Router Deployment Pending Testing
news.summary: Thirteen senators want the FAA to halt a nationwide network router upgrade after a near five-hour ground stop scrubbed more than 18,000 flights.
news.why: Shippers relying on belly-hold and express air should build a day of buffer into time-critical shipments until the FAA's network rollout is stabilized.

news.title: Fate of Hormuz Remains in Limbo Following Midterm Sweep for Democrats
news.summary: Iran is holding out for seven U.S. concessions before loosening its grip on the Strait of Hormuz, even as Brent slid below $95 after the midterms and October proved the worst month yet for ship attacks.
news.why: Energy-linked surcharges may ease with crude, but buyers should not lock in long-term fuel assumptions until the December 11 U.S. funding deadline clarifies policy.

news.title: South Korean Carrier Weighs Selling Ship After First Arctic Journey
news.summary: PanStar's 2,758-TEU trial ship ran the Northern Sea Route at roughly a quarter full and with no return cargo, and the owner is now considering selling or chartering it out.
news.why: The Arctic shortcut is still not a practical Asia–Europe option, so plan around Suez and Cape routings for 2027 contracts.

news.title: EU Targets Shadow Fleet Shipowners, Managers and Insurers in New Russia Sanctions
news.summary: Brussels' latest Russia sanctions package goes after the owners, managers, insurers and financiers that keep Moscow's shadow tanker fleet operating.
news.why: Companies chartering tankers or buying refined products should re-screen vessels and counterparties against the updated EU lists to avoid compliance exposure.

news.title: UKMTO Reports Two Tanker Attacks in Strait of Hormuz
news.summary: Two tankers caught fire in their engine rooms after separate attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, leaving one vessel without propulsion.
news.why: Gulf-bound cargo will keep carrying war-risk premiums, so importers sourcing from the region should confirm insurance terms and allow extra transit time.

news.title: Cargo Ship Capsizes Off Bulgaria After Reported Sea Drone Attack
news.summary: A Somali-flagged vessel loaded with close to 3,000 tonnes of wheat overturned in the Black Sea after its crew reported being hit by two sea drones.
news.why: Grain and agri-commodity buyers should expect Black Sea freight and insurance costs to rise as attacks spread toward EU coastal waters.

news.title: Suez Canal Return Won't Resolve Global Shipping Congestion, DHL Warns
news.summary: DHL cautions that capacity freed by carriers returning to Suez will be partly absorbed by stubborn port congestion and network disruption.
news.why: Don't bank on an immediate drop in Asia–Europe rates or transit times; keep safety stock until schedule reliability actually improves.

news.title: Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd Expand Suez Canal Return With Three More Gemini Services
news.summary: The Gemini partners are shifting three additional loops back to the Red Sea and Suez routing, extending the industry's step-by-step return.
news.why: Shippers on Gemini lanes should check updated port rotations and ETAs, since shorter voyages can bring cargo in earlier than booked.

news.title: Supertanker Rates Plunge More Than 60% From Record Highs
news.summary: Earnings for the biggest crude carriers have collapsed since early November as charter demand softened and October's geopolitical risk premium unwound.
news.why: Lower crude transport costs should filter into fuel and petrochemical input prices over the coming weeks, a modest relief for energy-intensive buyers.

news.title: UK Moves Toward New Maritime Fuel Standard
news.summary: Britain has launched a consultation on rules that would gradually force ships calling at UK ports to cut the carbon intensity of the fuel they burn.
news.why: Expect carriers to pass compliance costs on through new surcharges on UK-bound freight once the standard is finalized.

news.title: FedEx launches China-US air capacity ahead of peak season
news.summary: FedEx is adding weekly flights linking Shanghai and Guangzhou factories with U.S. gateways, aimed largely at AI hardware demand.
news.why: Electronics importers gain another express option for urgent peak-season China freight, which may help cap transpacific air rates.

news.title: BMW opens South Carolina battery plant; highlights 'local for local' supply chain strategy
news.summary: BMW's new Woodruff, S.C. facility assembles Gen6 batteries for the iX5 and leans on more than 200 Southeastern suppliers, with cell sourcing set to move to Arizona later this decade.
news.why: Tier-two and tier-three suppliers in the Southeast have a growing opening to win automotive business as BMW expands its Americas supplier base past 850 sites.
